authentication.credential_handling: The receiver emits into the local logs pipeline; egress authentication is the pipeline's existing exporter configuration.

known_blind_spots: Coverage is the loaded audit ruleset: auditd emits only what rules request, so an unloaded syscall class records nothing and a hostile operator can clear rules unless audit lock (auditctl -e 2) is set.
Attribution to a logical agent is inferred by pid/ppid/auid and time — fork-heavy or namespace-churned workloads degrade it; container-scoped filtering needs the eBPF emitter (spec 031).
file_access (openat) is high-volume on real systems and disabled by default; enabling it without scoped rules can exceed emit and queue budgets.
Very short-lived processes and io_uring-driven syscalls can evade the audit pipeline on some kernels; auditd's own blind spots carry through.
manage_rules writes audit rules only when no daemon holds the control socket; a running auditd wins and its ruleset governs what we see.
Records are host-level metadata (process, peer, path hash), not agent intent — the semantic layer still requires SDK or framework instrumentation.

Netlink failed deliveries use bounded in-memory retry and multicast cannot replay missed kernel events. Logfile mode requires persistent private state and source retention: staged scrubbed batches are restart-replayable, while removed pre-stage source generations, ambiguous rotation and kernel/auditd loss remain unknown gaps. Next-consumer acceptance is not remote durable acknowledgement; at-least-once replay requires destination deduplication by stable record ID.

authentication.credential_handling: Outbound header and TLS credentials can be mounted from operator-created Kubernetes Secrets or Compose secrets; bearer-token ingress is wired by the compose production overlay and mTLS by the production Helm profile.

known_blind_spots: The pinned bearertokenauth extension (v0.150.0) splits token files on newlines and retains empty entries, so a blank line or trailing newline mints an empty "Bearer " credential that gRPC metadata preserves; preflight-prod.sh rejects unsafe files, fabric-gate refuses them at boot and while running (the extension re-reads via fsnotify), verify-prod.sh re-checks them, and an upstream patch is prepared under components/otel-collector-fabric/upstream/.
The production chart supports mTLS ingress, but does not bind asserted telemetry identity attributes to a verified workload identity.
The receiver cannot observe agent activity that was never emitted by upstream instrumentation.

Shipped configurations are limited to traces and logs pipelines; the fabric-gate image entrypoint refuses to boot a config defining any other pipeline, and qualify-distribution-config.sh proves the refusal. Operators who build or wrap their own collector binary lose that enforcement and must re-apply the qualification gate.
Bounded free-form caller metadata, including interaction kinds and tool names, crosses the boundary verbatim and is not semantic content; destinations should treat it as asserted-unverified metadata.
The recorder preserves protected OTLP and does not materialize Activity Envelope v2, privacy assertions, or delivery receipts; a downstream adapter or destination must provide those contracts.
The default development exporter is local stdout, not durable evidence storage or a compliance posture; the production profile requires an authenticated TLS destination.
Persistent queues provide bounded at-least-once transport and cannot prove backend retention or exactly-once delivery.
Metadata allowlisting occurs after the agent and model interaction and cannot prevent raw PII from reaching an LLM.

authentication.credential_handling: The emitter optionally reads a bearer-token file or a client certificate/key pair. TLS is the default; an explicit development-only insecure transport setting rejects bearer tokens and TLS files.

known_blind_spots: Cannot identify prompts, completions, tool arguments, tool results, policy verdicts, or decision boundaries — kernel metadata only.
Requires CAP_BPF+CAP_PERFMON and kernel >=5.8 with BTF; the container runs read-only mounts and refuses to start on kernels that lack support.
Encrypted traffic prevents payload or trace-header inspection — peer/timing metadata only.
openat (file_access) is host-scale volume and off by default; enabling it without cgroup scoping can exceed emit budgets.
Attribution to a logical agent depends on correct cgroup_path; all_host=true is an explicit opt-in and widens collection to the whole node.
An adversarial workload with kernel-level access is outside this threat model — the emitter observes the host it runs on and cannot defend the kernel itself.
The emitter has a bounded fsynced source spool with at-least-once replay and stable record IDs, but neither source fsync nor OTLP acceptance proves durable destination storage.
Spool exhaustion causes a visible sensor stop; activity while the sensor is down or before a kernel loss count is durably queued cannot be reconstructed by this source.
Only configured tracepoints and cgroup scope are observed; kernel ring-buffer loss and partial argv/path capture require explicit incomplete status and independent reconciliation.
